questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place and a culture I had never experienced before. I have been to USA before, but only north and wanted to try something more southern. It was also crucial to be able to have the classes that interested me and aligned with my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely loved my stay and would recommend it to anyone. I did not have a bad week and the atmosphere was awesome.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Could have been better. Ended up being there before the intro days for exchange students as I wanted to settle in correctly (came Tuesday and intro was Thursday). Because of this "early arrival" I had to pay an additional fee of $50 - nothing that ruins the budget, but could have been avoided with better information. 
Be aware that school does not start until a week later and do not stress about being there early as American students do not move in until the weekend.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Had help from the counter, who showed me my room and were always helpful with whatever info I needed. This includes busses to center of campus etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of different intro dates from different e-mails. I did miss a orientation meeting as I got lost in all the mails. Nothing too serious and was easy to recover the information :)

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A lot of options. The 1st month I lived in a studio, which was on main campus, but around 25-30 min walk from my apartment. I did move later on to a dorm on central campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were both meal plans available and cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
As an exchange student I would recommend living on a dorm. I moved from a studio where I lived alone, with a shower, kitchen and decent space, to a small dorm room, which I know sounds like a weird turn around for most. This was just a lot more social, you live with other exchange students as well (in the building) and it was a part of international program, which means I got to live with an American who I got along with really well. I know my friends who was also on exchange also got along well with their roommates. Bathroom facilities were good and nothing to worry about, which I know I did. Furthermore you were able to cook in the basement with lots of space. 
I had a really good time at my studio apartment, but I recommend going to Alexander Hall, which is centrally located and really social.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy to find classes and what was available. Exchange students were prioritized a little, so it was easy to get your classes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Wished for some classes I had picked out beforehand. When registration opened I found out I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Good communication with one of the corresponders.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Was perfect.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure you have access to the classes you need for your studies. There are some classes only provided during spring semester and same way around for the fall semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academics were really good and professors were nice to help with whatever. Academically it did not require as much effort as you may be used to, but still a satisfying level. If you are going entirely academics, it could have been a higher level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had three 400 classes, which means last year of their undergrad. One 300 and one 200 online class. 
I had a finance class, where I did not quite have all the prerequisites for, but was by far my favorite class - I recommend taking classes you just find interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH we are used to having a lecture and in class. At NCSU we only had one in class, which were combinations of lectures and activities.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ressource and environmental economics 
Game Theory
Financial management of corporations
Personal finance
International finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Financial management of corporations was my favorite course. Professor was nice and I really enjoyed the overall material in the class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Extra housing fees, extra payment fees (credit card fees).
Early check in fee, because miscommunication. 
Student Visa and especially fees applying for this. 
Immunizations record and fees within this - I did not encounter having to get extra vaccinations, but this occurred to multiple of my friend. 
Health insurance can become expensive, I was fortunate enough it was not for me.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing fees and visa was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Joined the XC running team, which was good fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and so on was available - you could even start your own if you wanted to. We were presented to a website with all of them upon arrival.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports team to socialize with Americans, as this can be a little harder to do otherwise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mountains and beach areas. Renting a car it is beneficial to know someone 25 y/o or more, as it is cheaper.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just don't be shy and join the conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the everyday food takes some time. Healthy food can be a bit more expensive/not accessible.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of Americans.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Move to a dorm
2) Join as many social events as possible
3) Make friends in all of your classes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be shy to use the facilities as these are open to everyone.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friends and academics. Still talk to multiple other exchange students from different countries, and even visited each other.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to cultural differences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
